description: The THROUGH range's [ IN alphabet-name-1 ] phrase - ISO 14.9.13.2's range-expression (EVALUATE WHEN) and 13.18.63.2 formats 3 and 5 (the condition-name VALUE clause), governed together by 14.7.8 rule 2 ('When the IN alphabet-name phrase is specified, the collating sequence used for range evaluation is the collating sequence defined by that alphabet'). A COBOL-2002 addition - DERIVED, not quoted: the 2023 Annex E covers 2014->2023 only and lists no range/collation delta, so the phrase is present by 2014; the repo holds no 2002 or 2014 text; COBOL-85's EVALUATE and VALUE formats carry a bare THROUGH pair ordered by the program collating sequence, and 14.7.8 rule 2's own NOTE ('to allow an implementor to define the collating sequence in a manner compatible with previous COBOL implementations') and its locale arm (LC_COLLATE - the locale facility, LOCALE reserved from 2002 per reserved-words.json) place the phrase with 2002's collation rework. Gated at the ONE resolver both formats reach, SpecialNamesBinder.TryResolveRangeAlphabet (kb/Work PB1015), because the phrase is decided by SYMBOL, not by position: IN is an optional word (kb/Work PB983) and an EVALUATE identifier-4 IN word parses as a qualification until the binder peels it (PB843), so no parse-arm recognition can see every spelling. Fires only once the word IS an alphabet-name (a word naming no alphabet is not the phrase).
display: the THROUGH range's IN alphabet-name phrase
vcr: THROUGH range IN alphabet-name-1 phrase (COBOL-2002, derived); A1 authority-sufficiency gap (D18); kb/Work PB1015
source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. VMRNGIN.
ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
CONFIGURATION SECTION.
SPECIAL-NAMES.
    ALPHABET AL IS NATIVE.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 WS-C PIC X VALUE "C".
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN.
    EVALUATE WS-C
        WHEN "A" THRU "M" IN AL DISPLAY "IN"
        WHEN OTHER DISPLAY "OUT"
    END-EVALUATE.
    STOP RUN.
